verdicts.why: Describes the far-past-expected degree of the gloss and places the word as the admiring member of its family; positive charge is plausible and the hedge 'can flatter' accommodates the mildly critical Austen examples.
Flat measurement of distance from the norm with no verdict matches the gloss and the neutral charge; examples fit.
Positional, verdict-free reading fits 'beyond a norm in opinion or actions', the neutral charge, and the example 'the far right'.
Formal register and a cooler-than-unreasonable disapproval fit 'beyond normal limits' and the negative charge; the note is relative, not a claim of no verdict.
Excess treated as an affront demanding objection matches 'greatly exceeding bounds of reason or moderation' and the negative charge; example fits.
Opinions and actions well past the norm by commitment, eyed with reserve, stays inside the gloss and supports a mild negative charge.
Reads the degree sense (a sinful waste) correctly as excess framed as a wrong, contrasted with extraordinary under the same gloss; negative charge fits.
'Complete or extreme with nothing softening it' is the gloss; the bleak, unrelieved colour is the intensifier's own force in 'stark poverty' and 'stark contrast', and neutral is plausible.
Informal register label plus a grumble-sized overshoot fits the 'steep prices' sense under this gloss and the negative charge.

The note describes a bare positional intensifier that 'says nothing about it beyond how far out it sits' — the same verdict-free force as far, which is labelled neutral — yet the charge is negative; note and charge contradict each other and one must be repaired.
Faulting the excess as unwarranted rather than bulky fits 'beyond normal limits', the negative charge, and the 'undue elegance' example.
Overstepping convicted of having no argument for itself is inside the gloss, heavier than excessive, and the negative charge fits 'unreasonable demands'.
Mild fondness measured against a young boy, covering both 'befitting' and 'characteristic of', matches the gloss and the positive charge; 'a boyish grin' fits.
Neutral intensifier pushing youth to its beginning fits 'very young' and 'at an early age'.
Classificatory sorting by who is included or aimed at is exactly 'including or intended for youthful persons'; neutral charge and examples fit.
Endearing warmth in the young child or animal, contrasted with small's plain measurement, fits the gloss and the positive charge; examples fit.
Plain, unsentimental sizing of the same young creature fits the gloss and the neutral charge; 'small children' fits.
Youth as breakable softness rather than admired quality fits 'young and immature' and 'at a tender age'; neutral-in-family is plausible.
Literary register label and admiration of vigour fit 'suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh' and the positive charge.
Counting vigour and freshness rather than years is precisely the 'suggestive of youth' sense; both examples ('young for his age', 'step was still young') fit it, and the positive charge is plausible.
Hedged, approximate granting of youth fits 'somewhat young'; 'faintly grudging' is colour, not a charge contradiction, and neutral is plausible.
Youth as resemblance with freshness carrying the claim matches 'suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh' and the positive charge.
Desertion framed as broken trust against the one left behind fits 'prove undependable to; abandon, forsake' and the negative charge.
Hopes or expectations coming up short, with no abandonment, is the gloss; the Austen examples fit and negative charge is right.
Not being there when relied on, covering both halves of the gloss and stated as a lapse, fits 'courage did not fail her' and the negative charge.
Want of power turned into a judgement fits 'lacking in power or forcefulness', the negative charge, and 'an ineffectual ruler'.

Plain naming of the missing power below ineffectual's verdict fits the gloss; negative is plausible because the gloss itself names a deficiency, and both examples show the adjectival power-lacking sense.
Unshowy praise locating depth in the thinking itself fits 'marked by depth of thinking', the positive charge, and all three examples.
